findings: Cached-result validation checks File(item.id).exists, length and modification time truncated to whole seconds. Same-size edits within one second or restored timestamps can retain old groups; there is no content or physical identity validation.
Loading retains unscannableFiles unchanged without existence/metadata validation. It filters groups to two surviving members but does not recompute signatures or similarity.

Similarity denial keys join sorted paths with unescaped | and use this as primary key. Distinct path pairs can collide before storage if IDs permit the delimiter; separate pathA/pathB columns do not disambiguate replacement.
Denials are tied to path strings rather than content identity or recipe, so changed/replaced files at the same paths remain denied. DAO offers insertion and getAll only; no invalidation shown.
addSimilarityDenials eagerly constructs every unordered pair, quadratic in group size, with no visible group limit or cancellation checkpoint. Actual large-group memory use unmeasured.
hideGroupId performs read-modify-write on a SharedPreferences set without repository-level synchronization. Concurrent additions can overwrite each other; no concurrency runtime control yet.
